title: MLCC Deployment-Target Descriptor
description: Per-deployment-target descriptor. The single source of truth for a target's contract (status var, success status, config schema, verb applicability). The scattered authorities (do/config template, _guard_deployment_active, do-config.js SHELL_VAR_TO_ANSWER, regenerate RUNTIME_OWNED_VARS, the deploy/clean dispatchers, deploy_schema.py) DERIVE from these descriptors instead of hardcoding per-target knowledge. See ADR-008.

target.description: Canonical target key; matches the descriptor directory name (e.g. realtime-inference, eks).

aliases.description: Backward-compatible alias names that normalize to `target` (e.g. managed-inference -> realtime-inference). Empty [] when none.

status_var.description: The per-target state variable written to do/config on deploy success/failure. Read by _guard_deployment_active.

answer_key.description: The camelCase generator-answer key for status_var, used by do-config.js SHELL_VAR_TO_ANSWER.

success_status.description: The status_var value that means 'active' for this target. Must be one of the states _guard_deployment_active accepts.

family.description: Deployment family. sagemaker-endpoint: real-time/async managed endpoints. sagemaker-job: batch transform. kubernetes: served as k8s pods (hyperpod-eks via the operator, eks without it).

deploy_script.description: Path (relative to do/) of the deploy dispatcher target script.

clean_script.description: Path (relative to do/) of the teardown target script.

required_vars.description: Config vars that must be non-empty before deploy (deploy_schema.py SCHEMAS.required).

optional_vars.description: Optional config vars with their default values (deploy_schema.py SCHEMAS.optional).

runtime_owned_vars.description: Vars this target writes at runtime that `mcc regenerate` must PRESERVE (feed regenerate's RUNTIME_OWNED_VARS). Always includes status_var; add any other per-target runtime-written vars. Cross-target/global runtime vars (VLLM_*, HP_SPECULATIVE_*, benchmark, mlflow) stay in the shared set, not here.

serving_config_source.description: Which resolve-serving-config.sh resolution arm this target uses. kubernetes: reads HP_*/BENCHMARK_* (hyperpod-eks, eks). sagemaker-ic: reads DEPLOYED_INSTANCE_TYPE/IC_ENV_* (realtime, async, batch).

adapter_delivery.description: Wave 6.1 (R1.1, BL189): how LoRA adapters reach the serving pod on this target, so do/adapter and the deploy driver derive the mapping instead of hardcoding it. strategy model-prefix: the adapter lives under <model S3 prefix>/<subdir>/<project>/<name>/ and the pod sees it at <mount_path>/<subdir>/<project>/<name> through the S3 model mount (hyperpod-eks with prefetchEnabled: false; eks with EKS_MODEL_MOUNT=s3). Omit on targets that load adapters another way (realtime-inference adapter ICs).

cluster_contract.description: Wave 8 (R5.3): the READ-ONLY cluster-contract preflight do/validate runs for this target (kubernetes family), so the dispatcher derives which helper to call instead of branching on the target name. script: path relative to do/. A .sh script is sourced in a subshell and `entry` (a shell function) is called: exit 0 = satisfied, non-zero = a contract miss (its output is the finding). A .py script is run as `python3 <script> <entry>` and prints {"findings": [{severity, check, message, fix}]}. The deploy driver calls the same helper; validate never mutates anything.

service_quota_usage.description: Wave 8 (right-sizing `quota` check): the SageMaker Service Quotas usage suffix this target's instances count against, e.g. 'endpoint usage' (quota name '<instance> for endpoint usage') or 'transform job usage'. Omit on targets whose capacity is cluster-provided (kubernetes family); the quota check then reports skip.

pricing.description: Wave 9 (R7.1, R8.2): how the price resolver (do/lib/python/pricing.py) prices this target's instances. service: the AWS Price List service code. component: the AmazonSageMaker `component` attribute value (Task 1, live GetProducts 2026-10-26: Hosting = real-time endpoints, AsyncInf = async endpoints, BatchTransform = transform jobs, Cluster = HyperPod); omitted for AmazonEC2 (EC2 uses the fixed Linux / Shared / NA / Used filter set). instance_count: how many instances one benchmark run is billed for.

instance_count.description: basis endpoint-current: DescribeEndpoint ProductionVariants[0].CurrentInstanceCount at write time. basis replicas: nodes occupied = ceil(<replicas_var> x <gpus_per_replica_var> / catalog GPUs per instance); a gpus_per_replica value of 'auto' means the whole instance. basis not-benchmarked: do/benchmark refuses this target, so no count is derived.

compute_backends.description: Wave 11 (R1.1, OQ-11.5): the training compute backends do/train and do/tune may submit to from a project on this target, in preference order; the FIRST entry is the default when --backend is not given. smtj = a SageMaker training job (every target). hp-eks = a single-node HyperPodPyTorchJob on the project's HyperPod EKS cluster (hyperpod-eks only; opt-in, never the default). Verbs read this at run time through target_manifest.py compute_backends; no consumer branches on the target name.

scale_to_zero.description: Wave 10 (ADR-014 §1/§2, R1): whether and how this target can scale to zero, and whether MLCC wires it in this release. do/deploy flag acceptance (--scale-to-zero), the cold-start warning wording, do/status and do/clean derive from this block instead of branching on the target name. support: what the platform offers (native = the AWS service scales the billed capacity to zero; pod-only = pods scale but nodes stay billed; requires-cluster-addon = needs an add-on the cluster owner installs; not-applicable = the target never idles). The enums are an open set: extend them here when a new target needs a new value. mechanism: the plug-point do/lib/scale-to-zero.sh dispatches on (ADR-013 style), null when there is none. wake_signal: the metric that wakes the target from zero, null when unknown. requests_at_zero: what a request sees while at zero (fail / queued / unknown / n/a); it drives the warning text. idle_billing: what is still billed at zero. enabled: MLCC v2 wires it (only with support native plus a mechanism and wake signal); reason: why not, shown verbatim when --scale-to-zero is refused.

verbs.description: Per-verb applicability for verbs that are target-restricted. true = the verb applies to this target; false = the verb refuses it (exit 3). Only verbs that vary by target need listing (optimize, add-ic, ci, adapter, draft, metrics). Verbs with `targets: all` are not listed.

add-pod.description: Wave 11 (R8.1, BL149): do/add-pod applies (the ADR-013 contract derives a pod-apply mechanism for full_model on this target). Must agree with _additive_verb_supported_on add-pod (additive-deploy-contract.test.js).

metrics.description: Wave 9 (OQ-9.9): do/metrics applies (the target has an observability store). Must equal observability.store != 'none'. Unlike the other verbs, do/metrics on a target where this is false prints a skip notice with the reason and exits 0 (R12.4) instead of a contract violation.

observability.description: Wave 9 (R1, R6, R12; ADR-008): where this target's serving metrics live and how to select them, so gpu_metrics.py (benchmark Phase 1 / AMP), endpoint_metrics.py (do/metrics) and do/status derive the store, label selector and dashboard pointer instead of branching on the target name. store cloudwatch-promql: SageMaker AI detailed observability, PromQL at monitoring.<region>.amazonaws.com/api/v1/query (SigV4 monitoring). store amp: the HyperPod observability add-on's Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace (SigV4 aps), discovered via amp_discovery. store none: no AWS-native store; benchmark falls back to the engine scrape when `fallback` says so.

histogram_form.description: native: histograms are OTel exponential (query the bare name). classic: Prometheus _bucket series with an `le` label.

selector.description: Role -> PromQL label name for the engine series (roles: endpoint, variant, inference_component, deployment, namespace). Values are supplied at query time from the project config.

gpu_selector.description: Role -> PromQL label name for the DCGM GPU series, when they carry different labels than the engine series (HyperPod DCGM uses `container`).

fallback.description: engine-scrape: when the store is absent or returns no series, use the opt-in port-forward /metrics poller sidecars (HP_BENCHMARK_METRICS_ENABLED).

dashboard.description: The native AWS dashboard do/metrics and do/status point at.

amp_discovery.description: store amp only: the EKS add-on whose configurationValues JSON names the AMP workspace (dotted key path to the Prometheus endpoint URL) and, optionally, the AMG workspace name.

copy_concurrency.description: Classic CloudWatch metric for per-copy concurrency (do/metrics readout), read with GetMetricData.

answer_params.description: The single source of truth for this target's deploy answer-key plumbing (see docs/adr/ADR-008 and .kiro/steering/derive-dont-hardcode.md). Each entry ties an answer key (DEPLOY_ANSWERS JSON key) to its config var, optional CLI flag, and roles. The four historical tables — CLI_FLAG_TO_VARS (deploy-config-builder.js), flag_to_answer_key (.deploy_helper.py), _ANSWER_KEY_TO_VAR (deploy_prompts.py), and the inline KEY_MAP (do/deploy) — plus do/deploy's flag arg-parse arms and both forwarding blocks all DERIVE from the union of these per-target arrays. Option B: every target lists all its params independently (including core target/instance_type) so a target can add or target-scope a param without touching a shared table; a conformance test enforces that any answerKey shared across targets maps to the same configVar.

configVar.description: The SCREAMING_SNAKE config/env var the answer key resolves to.

flag.description: The CLI flag (do/deploy) that supplies this value. Present only for roles that include flag-input.

roles.description: flag-input: has a CLI flag; appears in builder/helper flag tables, do/deploy arg-parse arms, and both forwarding blocks. prompt-core: the core target/instance_type params handled specially by the builder but still answer keys on the Python side. internal: no flag; produced by prompts/builder; part of the DEPLOY_ANSWERS input surface (_ANSWER_KEY_TO_VAR). builder-output: emitted only in the Node builder's JSON output (do/deploy KEY_MAP); no flag, no prompt input. input-only: a flag/prompt/internal param the builder does NOT re-emit, so it is excluded from the output KEY_MAP (e.g. endpoint_name, re-emitted target-scoped as smai_/async_endpoint_name; hp_instance_group_name).
